audit.report: Checkout degraded to 55-79% success (vs 95% SLO) when a refund_batch_settle settlement worker held an idle transaction (SELECT 1) for 4.2s, blocking sessions. The database guardian initially proposed terminating the blocker based on memory of similar replayable jobs, but probes revealed it is a PROTECTED_SETTLEMENT job (never_interrupt, non-replayable) that settles approved customer refunds with the payment processor. Trade-off analysis showed waiting ~41s would cost ~$2,654 in revenue but fit within the business's 60s degradation tolerance, so both guardians agreed to wait. The blocker finished on its own immediately (0s wait), and checkout recovered to 100% success (36/36) within the verification window. The business is verified recovered: database clear, checkout SLO met, and protected operations intact.
audit.root_cause: A refund_batch_settle settlement worker held an idle transaction (last statement SELECT 1) for 4.2s, causing lock contention that degraded checkout to 55-79% success vs 95% SLO.
lessons: For refund_batch_settle workload: Add monitoring and alerting on idle-in-transaction duration for settlement_worker processes, since they are PROTECTED_SETTLEMENT (never_interrupt) and cannot be terminated even when blocking checkout.

For refund_batch_settle workload: Investigate why the settlement worker went idle in transaction (last statement SELECT 1) — likely an application bug or connection pool issue — to prevent future lock contention.
For refund_batch_settle workload: Since it is non-replayable and never_interrupt, consider reducing its lock footprint or scheduling it during lower-traffic windows to minimize blast radius.
audit.negotiation_critique: The database guardian initially proposed termination based on memory of similar replayable jobs but correctly pivoted after probes revealed the PROTECTED_SETTLEMENT/never_interrupt invariant; the continuity guardian accepted the wait decision after trade-off analysis confirmed the cost fit within tolerance. Agreement was reached in 1 round with no wasted rounds or missed evidence.
follow_ups: Root cause analysis on why refund_batch_settle worker went idle in transaction (SELECT 1) for 4.2s.
Add idle-in-transaction timeout or monitoring for settlement_worker processes.
Review settlement worker connection pool settings to prevent idle transactions.

events.title: R1 proposes escalate

proposal.rationale: The root blocker is a settlement_worker (refund_batch_settle) idle in transaction for 4.2s (DB-1). Checkout success is 55-77% vs 95% SLO with $4,293/min at risk (TEL-1, BIZ-1). Memory shows terminating similar batch_replayable_* jobs restored checkout (MEM-1), but refund_batch_settle is a settlement worker — different domain, unknown replayability. Critical evidence missing: workload_registry (replayability/interrupt policy), protected_settlements (in-flight card settlements), tradeoff (cost of wait vs interrupt), change_calendar. Cannot safely terminate without knowing if refund_batch_settle is replayable or has protected settlements. Cannot wait blindly with 60s tolerance. Escalation with decision brief informed by requested probes is appropriate.

proposal.risk_assessment: Delay of probe execution (seconds) consumes part of 60s tolerance. If probes reveal refund_batch_settle is non-replayable or has protected settlements, terminate could cause financial inconsistency. If probes confirm replayable and no protected settlements, terminate likely safe per MEM-1 pattern.
